info.title: sf-mod-check
info.description: Read-only, offline checks of Starfield mods: plugin checks (structure, FormIDs, links, conditions, scenes, deleted and identical-to-master records), whole load-order conflicts, release-zip checks, and triage: a first-pass report on a downloaded mod. Formerly sfmodcheck.

options.name: --plugins
options.description: the load order (default: the game's own Plugins.txt); --mo2 reads an MO2 profile instead

options.name: --extra-data
options.description: a folder searched before Data for archives and loose files

options.name: --ini
options.description: another INI whose [Archive] lists and loose-file keys count (after Starfield.ini and StarfieldCustom.ini)

options.name: --language
options.description: the voice language whose archives load (default en); other languages' voice archives are skipped

options.name: --archives
options.description:
also search every .ba2 in this folder that the load order doesn't load (shown as not loaded;
they never win). Use it to search a mod's archives before it is installed.

options.name: --max
options.description: list at most this many file names (default 100; 0 lists them all). The counts stay complete.

options.name: --out
options.description: the folder to write to (made if it doesn't exist)

options.name: --force
options.description: overwrite files that already exist (default: an existing file is left alone and reported)

options.name: --max-size
options.description: the most the files may add up to, in GB (default 2). Checked before anything is written.

options.name: --ref
options.description: list the cell that holds this placed reference (where its winning copy sits), the reference marked

options.name: --near
options.description:
list the references within <radius> of the point (<x>, <y>) in the worldspace, nearest first, from
its persistent cell and every exterior cell. Distance is flat (X and Y; height is ignored) in the
game's units, and a reference exactly at the radius counts

options.name: --plugin
options.description:
read only this plugin (or the plugins of a .zip, .7z or .rar) and its masters, with no Plugins.txt;
give the cell as an EditorID or FormKey there (a console FormID needs the whole load order)

options.name: --max
options.description:
list at most this many references, and at most this many anchors (default 100; 0 lists them all);
the counts always cover every reference

options.name: --extra-data
options.description:
a folder, or a mod archive (.zip, .7z or .rar, unpacked to a temporary folder that is deleted afterwards);
its files win over the Data folder's, and a plugin in it that Plugins.txt doesn't list is read as the last plugin

options.name: --data
options.description: the game's Data folder, for the EditorIDs of records in the masters (default: Steam's usual folder)

options.name: --json
options.description:
the report as JSON instead of text (always complete); on stdout the RESULT line follows
the JSON, so use --out for a file that holds only the JSON

options.name: --out
options.description: write the report to this file (stdout then gets only the RESULT line)

options.name: --all
options.description:
list everything in the text report (long lists are cut short otherwise), and each cell's records
Records whose bytes differ but whose fields are all equal count as noise, which is no difference.
Scripts and script properties are matched by name, so a new order alone is noise.
exit 0 = no real differences (noise only counts as none), 1 = differences, 2 = bad input or setup

options.name: --out
options.description: the new plugin file; it must not exist yet, and it can't be the input

options.name: --drop-master
options.description: remove a master the plugin doesn't use (the FormIDs after it are renumbered); refused if anything uses it

options.name: --set-light
options.description: set the light flag; refused unless the plugin is full and its own records are 000800 to 000FFF

options.name: --set-text
options.description:
replace one line's text: an INFO's response text (NAM1) or a MESG's description (DESC), named by
EditorID, FormKey (000801:MyMod.esm) or console FormID. Give the new text with --text after it,
and --response <n> for an INFO's other responses (numbered from 1, as `find --full` shows them).
Repeat --set-text for more records (one line per record in a run). A localized plugin is
refused (its text is in .STRINGS files).

options.name: --data
options.description: the game's Data folder, for the masters (default: Steam's usual folder)

options.name: --masters-dir
options.description: look for masters here first (default: the plugin's own folder), then in the Data folder

options.name: --json
options.description: print one JSON object: the edits, each proof's result and whether the new file was kept

options.name: --quiet
options.description: leave out the tool's name and version line

options.name: --verbose
options.description: also print the log (each step and proof in detail) to stderr

options.name: --log
options.description: write that log to a file, for a bug report

options.name: --type
options.description: keep only records of this four-letter type, for example LCTN, MISC, NPC_

options.name: --plugin
options.description:
read only this plugin (or the plugins of a .zip, .7z or .rar) and their masters, with no Plugins.txt; with no record given, list every record
the plugin holds. Masters are looked for in the plugin's own folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data.
Give the record as an EditorID or FormKey: a console FormID needs the whole load order.

options.name: --masters-dir
options.description: another folder that holds the plugin's masters (can be given more than once)

options.name: --max
options.description:
with --plugin and no record: list at most this many records (default 100; 0 lists them all);
with --refs: list at most this many referring records (default 100; 0 lists them all)

options.name: --full
options.description:
print every nested value of the winning copy as an indented tree (zeros included) instead of the
main fields; --json adds it as "tree". On a dialogue topic (DIAL) it also lists the topic's lines
(INFOs): each one's winner and each response's number, text, emotion and face fields ("infos").
A sound GUID (SoundReference, WWED) also prints in the form a Wwise bank manifest uses
({XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}), so you can look it up in a sound bank's .json file

options.name: --versions
options.description:
list every copy of the record in load order and what each copy changes against the copy it was
built on; --json adds it as "versions" (needs a record: not with the --plugin listing)

options.name: --refs
--layout
options.description:
list the winning copy's subrecords as the file stores them, in order: offset, signature, size and a
short preview of the value (text, a number, or the first 16 bytes in hex); --json adds it as
"layout". A damaged record lists the subrecords before the bad spot and says what is wrong.
sf-mod-check find --type <SIG> --where "<field> <op> [<value>]" [--where ...] [--editorid-match <regex>]
[load-order options as above, or --plugin] [--max <n>] [--json] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
sf-mod-check find --editorid-match <regex> [--type <SIG>] [load-order options as above, or --plugin] [--max <n>] [...]

options.name: --where
options.description:
list every record of the --type whose winning copy matches (give no record to look up). <op> is
=  the value equals (a link: its EditorID, FormKey or console FormID; a number as a number)
!= it doesn't (an empty field counts as not equal)   ~  the value contains the text
has  the flag is set (Flags has Unique), or a list has the entry (Keywords has MyKeyword)
exists  the field isn't empty (no value after it; 0, false and no flag set count as empty)
The field is a name from find's fields block; a dotted path goes one level down per part
(Factions.Faction = MyFaction), and a list on the way matches when any entry does. Letter case is
ignored. Several --where are all required. An unknown field is refused with the type's field list.

options.name: --editorid-match
--data
options.description: the game's Data folder (default: Steam's usual folder)

options.name: --masters-dir
options.description: another folder to look for masters in (can be given more than once)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: no byline, and no WARNING lines when there are errors

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
the troubleshooting log on stderr, or in that file
The last line is RESULT: OK (0 errors, n warnings), RESULT: FAIL (n errors, n warnings) or RESULT: CANNOT CHECK (...).
exit 0 = no errors (warnings allowed), 1 = errors, 2 = can't check (a missing plugin or master, a bad argument)

options.name: --plugin
options.description: read only this plugin (or a .zip, .7z or .rar of plugins) and its masters (found in its folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data)

options.name: --compare
options.description:
count another NPC's lines per type too (for example a vanilla companion) and mark the types this
NPC has none of as missing; the same forms as the NPC

options.name: --type
options.description: keep only lines of this Category (Combat) or Category / Subtype ("Combat / Hit"); letter case ignored

options.name: --max
options.description: list at most this many lines (default 200; 0 lists them all); the counts are always complete

options.name: --no-files
options.description: don't look for the voice and lip files (faster; wem and lip show ?)

options.name: --json
options.description: print one JSON object with every line

options.name: --plugin
options.description:
a plugin (.esm, .esp or .esl) or a mod archive (.zip, .7z or .rar) read with its masters and no
Plugins.txt. Give it more than once to compare mods that aren't installed: each input's masters,
then the input, in the order given. When two inputs hold a plugin of the same name, the later one is
used; an input whose master isn't found is left out with a note and the rest run.

options.name: --type
options.description: only these record types, comma-separated four-letter signatures: DIAL,INFO

options.name: --min
options.description: list a record when at least this many non-official plugins hold it (default 2; 1 with --records)

options.name: --records
options.description:
a text file of records to look up ("who edits these"): one FormKey (064F3C:Starfield.esm) or console
FormID (0001295A) per line; # lines and blank lines are skipped. Only the plugins that may hold them
are read, and the official copies are listed too (marked official)

options.name: --max
options.description: list at most this many records (default 200; 0 lists them all)

commands.name: check
commands.description: (is a patch still up to date? sf-mod-check patch check --help)

options.name: --plugin
options.description: read only this plugin (or a .zip, .7z or .rar of plugins) and its masters, and show only the scenes the plugin adds or changes

options.name: --hub
options.description: the talk menu scene (EditorID or FormKey), when the one found by counting jumps is wrong

options.name: --out
options.description: write the tree to this Markdown file and print only the counts

options.name: --max
options.description: show at most this many scenes (default 50; 0 shows them all); the problems and stages are always complete

options.name: --json
options.description: print one JSON object instead

options.name: --max
options.description:
examples listed per type and per field (default 5), and cells listed per worldspace (default 20);
0 lists them all. --json always lists every cell.

options.name: --out
options.description: write the list to this file (default: the screen, stdout)

options.name: --voice
options.description: a voice type (EditorID) for the lines that name none; may be given more than once

options.name: --utf8
options.description:
write UTF-8 (default: Windows-1252, what the Creation Kit writes and Voice Cloner reads;
a UTF-8 file needs SVC_EXPORT_ENCODING=utf-8 set on the Voice Cloner side)
